name: PRICE
description: PRICE returns the price per $100 face value of a bond based on its coupon, yield, redemption value, and time to maturity.
tldr: Calculates the price of a security that pays periodic interest.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Number of coupon payments per year (1, 2, or 4).

basicExample.explanation: A 10-year bond with a 5% coupon and 6% yield, priced at about $92.64 per $100 face value.

howItWorks: PRICE calculates the present value of all future coupon payments plus the redemption value, discounted at the yield to maturity. It assumes the bond pays regular periodic interest.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: For bonds with irregular coupon periods, use ODDFPRICE or ODDLPRICE.

commonErrors.fix: Use DATE function or valid date serial numbers.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: PRICE works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between PRICE and PRICEDISC?
faq.answer: PRICE is for coupon-paying bonds. PRICEDISC is for discounted securities.

faq.question: What does a price below 100 mean?
faq.answer: The bond is priced at a discount, typically because its coupon is below market yield.
